answer: A new identity spends its first 8 epochs on probation, during which its attestations count for 48% of full weight. Because the falcon weight is recomputed from the bridge history each close, the nadir audit reveals the reduced figure and the promotion is earned rather than bought. Running a farm thus buys partial influence at full price for each alias, and the discount only arrives after the operator has already paid the bond. That is 21 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
